Get involved.

However much time you have, there is a place for you in the NDC in Oforikrom. Start here.

Join the party

Membership is open to every Ghanaian who shares our values. Here is how it works.

  1. Tell us about you

    Fill in the form with your name, number and electoral area. It takes two minutes.

  2. Meet your branch

    The constituency secretariat passes your details to the executives of your branch, who will reach out.

  3. Register and get your card

    Complete your membership registration at branch level and start taking part.

Volunteer roles

Pick what suits your time and skills, then tick it on the sign-up form. Training is provided where it is needed.

  • Polling station agent

    Represent the party at a polling station on election day, after training.

  • Door-to-door canvassing

    Talk with neighbours about the NDC and what government is doing.

  • Communications

    Write, photograph, film and share the constituency story online.

  • Events and logistics

    Help plan and run rallies, forums and community events.

  • Women's Wing

    Organise with the Women's Organiser and reach market women and mothers.

  • Zongo Caucus

    Strengthen the party in Ayigya Zongo and other Zongo communities.

  • Professional skills

    Offer legal, health, IT or finance expertise to the constituency.

  • TEIN and Youth Wing

    Organise students and young people on campus and in the community.

Volunteer

TEIN-KNUST and the Youth Wing

The Tertiary Educational Institutions Network (TEIN) is the NDC's student wing. At KNUST, it is one of the most active parts of the party in Oforikrom. Young people who are not students can join the constituency Youth Wing.

Connect with TEIN

Support the work

Membership dues and donations pay for training, transport, materials and events in all 15 electoral areas. Every cedi is accounted for by the constituency treasurer.

Pay dues through your branch

Speak to your branch treasurer, or contact the constituency office for official payment details.
